stories.headline: Ten Lead Changes, And The Last Unbeaten Survives
stories.dek: The Machines are 7-0 and spent the third quarter of this one losing. The lead changed hands six times in that quarter alone, and the best player on the field was wearing the other colours.
paragraphs: The Machines went to seven and oh by five and a half points, and for most of the afternoon they did not look like doing it. They led 42.56 to 37.60 at the interval, which was the only comfortable thing about the day, and then the third quarter happened: six lead changes in under four minutes of game time, the ball going back and forth between two teams who could not miss.

Bo Nix started it. With twelve minutes and forty-nine seconds left in the third he broke a sixty-two-yard touchdown run worth 12.20, the biggest single play of the game, and put the Killer Klowns in front 53.20 to 44.60. Thirty-nine seconds later Jared Goff threw sixteen yards for a touchdown and the Machines had it back. Michael Wilson caught fourteen to tie it at 54.70. Trey McBride caught twelve to untie it. Nix threw fifty-two for a touchdown and the Klowns led again at 63.10.

McBride settled it with eight minutes and fifty-seven seconds left in the third, a seven-yard touchdown catch that made it 70.70 to 68.10 and was the last time the lead moved. He finished with 17.10, Goff with 16.00, Amon-Ra St. Brown with 15.20. Bo Nix finished with 23.74 — more than anybody on either side — and lost.

Ryan Flournoy caught sixteen yards with fifty-two seconds left for 1.60, the sort of play that reads like a winner and was not: the margin had been 5.68 since the third quarter. The Klowns fall to 3-4. Two of the Machines' seven wins have come by under six points and they are the two narrowest of the set, 5.70 in week four and 5.68 here. The 97.82 is their second-lowest total of the season. What is carrying them is the other column: 534.86 conceded in seven weeks, the fewest in the league by 37.42, while sitting third on points scored.

stories.headline: A Hundred In A Half
stories.dek: Big Blue scored 100.80 points before the interval and 135.60 in all, the highest score of the week. Tony Pollard scored 33.50 for the other side and lost by fifty.
paragraphs: Eighteen touchdowns were scored in this game, more than in any other this week, and for about ten minutes of game time it was a fair fight. The lead changed four times in the first quarter. Tony Pollard ran thirty-six yards for a touchdown with five minutes and forty-seven seconds gone, worth 9.60, and Wookie Leaks led 12.00 to 5.30.

Then Big Blue stopped trading. Malik Willis threw seven yards for a touchdown to take it back, Chase Brown ran five with twenty-five seconds left in the first to make it 26.20 to 26.00, and that was the last time the game was close. By the interval it was 100.80 to 47.90.

Joe Burrow finished with 31.04, Malik Willis with 25.86, Tee Higgins 20.80, CeeDee Lamb 19.40 and Christian McCaffrey 16.00 — five men over sixteen. Lamb's sixteen-yard touchdown catch with forty-two seconds left was the last score of the game and nobody needed it.

Tony Pollard's 33.50 was the highest individual total in the game and one of the highest anywhere this week. Wookie Leaks are 2-5. Big Blue, who were 2-4 and have the third-highest points total in the league, are 3-4 and have now scored 135.60 and 160.42 in two of their seven weeks.

stories.headline: Six And Oh Becomes Six And One
stories.dek: The Beaver Eaters had not lost a game. Pork Chop Express led at half, were caught seven times before it, and won the second half as well.
paragraphs: The last unbeaten record outside the Machines went in a game that changed hands seven times before the interval and then stopped changing at all. D'Andre Swift ran one yard with fourteen minutes and six seconds left in the first to make it 0.70 to 0.60, which was the first of them, and Spencer Shrader's forty-three-yard field goal with nine minutes and sixteen seconds left in the second was the last.

Between those two the lead went back and forth on a Drake Maye seven-yard touchdown run, a Swift six-yard carry, a Maye forty-eight-yard touchdown pass worth 7.00 and a Baker Mayfield fourteen-yard touchdown throw. At the interval Pork Chop Express led 68.54 to 47.58 and the seesaw was over.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba's twenty-eight-yard touchdown catch eleven minutes into the fourth was worth 8.80, the biggest play of the game, and he finished with 22.30. Michael Penix Jr. had 22.24, D'Andre Swift 15.00, Saquon Barkley 13.10. For the Beaver Eaters, Drake Maye finished with 25.04 and Javonte Williams with 21.50.

Williams ran two yards for a touchdown with six seconds left, worth 6.20, which closed the margin to 20.36 and changed nothing. The Beaver Eaters are 6-1 and still have the most points in the league. Pork Chop Express are 6-1 as well, and they have the better of it on the head-to-head.

Pork Chop Express have not been under a hundred all season. Their lowest week is 100.22, in week four, and they are the only side in the league who can say it. The Beaver Eaters were next closest, and this was the game that took them under: 99.88, their own lowest of the year, in the week they stopped being unbeaten. They still lead the league on points scored with 867.44. The quarterbacks Pork Chop Express have started have cleared thirty points between them once in seven weeks.

stories.headline: Eighty-One Points Before The Interval
stories.dek: Horsecollars scored 81.70 in the first half and won by 68.38, the biggest margin of the week. Phins Phag's 54.82 was the lowest score anybody posted.
paragraphs: This was decided in about ten minutes of game time. Tyler Shough threw a one-yard touchdown pass with five minutes and thirty seconds left in the first to put Horsecollars ahead 9.10 to 7.10, the only lead change in the game, and they were never caught after it.

Zay Flowers caught forty-eight yards for a touchdown with two minutes and thirty-six seconds left in the first, worth 10.80. Jonathan Taylor ran thirty-eight for another with a minute and nineteen left, worth 9.80. By the interval it was 81.70 to 40.52, and Horsecollars had already scored more in a half than eleven teams managed in the whole week.
Geno Smith finished with 23.70, Flowers 19.70, Taylor 17.00, Blake Corum 16.10 and Brandon Aubrey 14.00. Aubrey's extra point with nineteen seconds left was the last score of the game.
Omar Cooper Jr. had 17.50 for Phins Phag and was the only man on that side in double figures until Jason Myers' 8.00. They are 1-6 and bottom of the league. Horsecollars are 5-2.

stories.headline: Level At The Interval, Forty-One Apart At The End
stories.dek: Six lead changes and a scoreline dead level at half. StillTheCream then won the second half 60.62 to 19.30.
paragraphs: At the interval this was 61.42 to 60.26 — a difference of 1.16 after thirty minutes in which the lead had already changed six times. Brock Purdy threw a one-yard touchdown to put the Powers of Pain ahead, Deshaun Watson ran nine for a touchdown to take it back, C.J. Stroud threw three yards to take it back again.
The last of the six came with nine minutes and twenty seconds left in the third, when Jordan Love threw fourteen yards for a touchdown and made it 71.60 to 65.70. Nothing after that was in doubt.

Rhamondre Stevenson's forty-eight-yard touchdown catch nine minutes into the first was the biggest play of the game at 10.80. Tre Tucker caught thirty-seven for a touchdown in the third worth 9.70 and finished with 16.30. Luther Burden III led everybody with 19.70, Stevenson had 17.50, Love 15.46, Watson 12.14.
C.J. Stroud finished with 17.50 for the Powers of Pain, Ashton Jeanty with 13.60 and Drake London with 12.60, and the side that was level at half scored 19.30 in the second.

part2.headline: First In The Spectre Syndicate, Eleventh In The League
part2.dek: The division changed hands on Sunday. StillTheCream took it off the side they had just beaten, and they hold it with fewer points than two of the three teams behind them.
paragraphs: The 122.04 is StillTheCream's best week of the season by 15.70, and a fourth win in a row after they lost the first three. What it takes is the Spectre Syndicate, off the side they beat to get it. The Powers of Pain had finished on top of that division at the end of six of the first seven weeks — every one but week three, when the Smoke Dragons held it — and they leave it by losing to the team that now has it. StillTheCream are 4-3, the Powers of Pain 3-4, the Guido Haters and the Smoke Dragons 2-5.

It is an odd sort of lead. StillTheCream have scored 585.94 points, eleventh in the league and third of the four sides in their own division: the Powers of Pain, a game behind them now, have 775.70. The first three weeks of the season brought them 177.26 points and no wins, including a 46.00 in week two that is still the second-lowest single week anybody has posted this year. The four weeks since have brought 408.68 and four wins. Nobody in the division is better than 4-3.

stories.headline: Three Men Over Twenty-Two, And It Was Over By Half
stories.dek: Lil' Chops led from the first score to the last and never once had it taken off them. Dak Prescott, Bucky Irving and Quinshon Judkins all cleared twenty-two points.
paragraphs: There were no lead changes in this game. Quinshon Judkins ran five yards for a touchdown with fourteen minutes and twenty seconds left in the first, and Lil' Chops led from then until the end.

Judkins ran six more for another with eight minutes and thirty-nine seconds left in the second, worth 6.60, and finished with 22.40. Bucky Irving had 23.00. Dak Prescott threw twenty-one yards for a touchdown in the fourth and finished with 25.04, the highest total on the field.
By the interval it was 73.94 to 32.20. Master-Jeti scored 25.70 in the second half and the margin never came under forty again.

Braelon Allen led Master-Jeti with 13.40 and Tez Johnson had 10.70, including a fourteen-yard touchdown catch with twelve seconds left in the second that was the biggest single play either side managed. Master-Jeti are 3-4. Lil' Chops are 4-3.

stories.headline: Forty Points Up At The Interval, And Beaten
stories.dek: The Smoke Dragons scored 72.30 in the first half and 6.90 in the second. The lead changed once all afternoon, with eight and a half minutes left.
paragraphs: At the interval the Smoke Dragons led 72.30 to 31.86, a margin of 40.44, and had scored more in a half than any side in the league bar Horsecollars. Colston Loveland had caught a twelve-yard touchdown in the first worth 7.20. Chase McLaughlin was kicking. Nothing about the first thirty minutes suggested what followed.

They scored 6.90 points in the second half. The Guido Haters scored 55.70. Josh Jacobs caught twenty-five yards for a touchdown with five minutes and thirty-one seconds left in the third, worth 8.50, and Kirk Cousins threw thirty-seven for another two minutes later.

The lead changed hands once, with eight minutes and thirty-one seconds left in the fourth, when Emanuel Wilson ran twenty-one yards for a touchdown worth 8.10 and made it 85.40 to 79.20. There was no answer: the Smoke Dragons' last points of the game had already been scored.

Cousins finished with 18.50, Wilson 17.50, Jacobs 15.10, Ja'Marr Chase 12.20. For the Smoke Dragons, Loveland and Kyler Murray tied on 12.90 and McLaughlin kicked 12.00. The Guido Haters, who had won once all season, are 2-5. So are the Smoke Dragons.

stories.headline: Eight Lead Changes, Then Both Sides Stopped
stories.dek: The lowest-scoring game of the week, and the one that would not settle: 133.96 points between them and eight changes of lead, six of them in the second quarter.
paragraphs: Kaelon Black ran thirty yards for a touchdown with thirteen minutes and eighteen seconds left in the second, worth 9.00 and the biggest play of the game, and n.W.o led 27.90 to 25.60. Over the following twelve minutes of game time the lead changed six more times.

George Kittle caught ten to put Gumbas ahead. KC Concepcion Jr. ran eighteen to take it back. Jauan Jennings caught twenty for Gumbas. Will Reichard kicked from fifty-two for n.W.o. Kittle caught twenty-one more with forty-nine seconds left in the half, and Gumbas led 54.80 to 53.20 at the interval.

Then it stopped. The two sides scored 25.36 points between them in the entire second half. Matthew Stafford threw eleven yards for a touchdown in the third, worth 6.20. The last score of the game came with seven minutes and thirty seconds left in the fourth and was worth 0.10.

Caleb Williams finished with 20.04 and Stafford with 19.60 for Gumbas, who are 3-4. KC Concepcion Jr. led n.W.o with 15.20 and Will Reichard kicked 13.00 — a kicker second on the team sheet. n.W.o are 2-5.

features.headline: Thirty-Seven Lead Changes
features.dek: Week seven would not settle. The lead changed hands thirty-seven times across the eight games — more than in any week this desk has rebuilt play by play — and three of the eight were won by the side that was behind at the interval.
paragraphs: There were thirty-seven lead changes in week seven. In week six there were twenty-three, in week five twenty-three, in week four twenty-six. Those are the four weeks that have been rebuilt from the tape, so it is the four that can be compared, and week seven is the busiest of them by eleven.

They were not spread evenly. The Machines and the Killer Klowns traded the lead ten times and six of those came inside four minutes of the third quarter. The Beaver Eaters and Pork Chop Express traded it seven times and every one came before the interval. Gumbas and n.W.o traded it eight times, six of them in the second quarter, and then scored 25.36 points between them after half.

Three games were won by the side losing at the interval. The Powers of Pain were 1.16 ahead at half and lost by 41.32. n.W.o were 1.40 ahead and lost by 12.36. And the Smoke Dragons were 40.44 ahead and lost by 8.36 — the second-largest halftime lead surrendered in the four weeks on record, behind the Killer Klowns' 61.40 in week four.

What all of that has not done is change the top of the table. The Machines won the closest game in the top half by 5.68 and are 7-0. The Beaver Eaters lost for the first time and are 6-1. Pork Chop Express beat them and are 6-1 too. Four of the sixteen have now won five or more; nine have won three or fewer; and the week that refused to settle anything left the order almost exactly as it found it.
